Remove outliers from training data using a convex hull polygon filter

bl_filter_outliers.Rd

In the standard workflow, outlier filtering is handled automatically by bl_prepare_data(hull_fraction = ...). Use bl_filter_outliers() directly only when you need to iterate on hull fractions without re-splitting the data (e.g., after bl_wrap_data()), or for other advanced use cases.

Usage

bl_filter_outliers(bl_data, hull_fraction = 0.9, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

bl_data

A "bl_data" object returned by bl_prepare_data() or bl_wrap_data().

hull_fraction

Numeric in (0, 1]; the fraction argument for aplpack::plothulls(). Values below 1 trim the most extreme points. 1.0 retains all points (no trimming). Default 0.9.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE, prints a one-line summary showing rows retained and removed with percentages. Default TRUE.

Value

A list of class "bl_filter_result" with components:

train_data

Filtered training data frame.

test_data

Test data frame (passed through unchanged; apply range filtering later via bl_project_points(..., filter_to_train_ranges = TRUE)).

var_names

Feature column names.

num_vars

Number of features.

target_class

The positive class value (passed through).

polygon

SpatialPolygons convex hull in standardised PCA space.

hull_fraction

The fraction value used.

n_retained

Number of training rows retained.

n_removed

Number of training rows removed.

Details

Projects training data into a lightweight 2-PC space, builds a convex hull enclosing hull_fraction of the points, removes observations outside the hull, and reports the number and percentage of rows retained and removed.

How the polygon filter works

The polygon is constructed in the standardised feature space (all variables centred and scaled), not in a biplot Z-space, so that it can be applied before the projection matrix is computed. The convex hull is computed using aplpack::plothulls() on the first two principal components of the raw feature matrix, which is a lightweight proxy for the full biplot projection.

Examples

# Standard workflow -- hull filtering integrated into bl_prepare_data()
bl_dat <- bl_prepare_data(datasets::iris,
                           class_col    = "Species",
                           target_class = "versicolor",
                           hull_fraction = 0.9)
#> Hull fraction: 0.90 | Retained: 110 (91.7%) | Removed: 10 (8.3%)
print(bl_dat)
#> <bl_filter_result>
#>   Hull fraction : 0.90
#>   Retained      : 110 (91.7%)
#>   Removed       : 10 (8.3%)
